gen_risks.description: Environmental impacts such as dust, noise, waste generation, and safety issues arising during physical construction of the central Citizen Service Center building.
gen_risks.mitigation: Execute all construction in accordance with a project-specific Environmental Management Plan (EMP) integrated into bidding documents and works contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: Operational policy OP 4.01 is triggered and the project categorized as a World Bank Category B because a new building will be constructed for CSC

gen_risks.description: Limited institutional and fiduciary implementation capacity in MIPA and the newly established ADISA agency to manage large donor-funded operations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated PMU under ADISA, hire qualified procurement and finance specialists, and provide structured operational training.
gen_risks.evidence: Neither MIPA, nor the recently constituted ADISA have previous experience in implementation of large donor funded operations

gen_risks.description: High procurement implementation risk due to ADISA being a newly created agency without fully established procurement staff or experience in Bank procedures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign interim procurement responsibilities to CFCU under MoF during the PPF period, recruit an experienced Procurement Specialist, and adopt a Project Operational Manual.
gen_risks.evidence: Since ADISA is a newly-created agency and the PMU is not yet fully set up, the procurement risk rating is high.

gen_risks.description: Substantial financial management risk stems from unintegrated accounting systems in non-budgetary agencies and lack of donor project FM experience.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire two financial reporting specialists, acquire dedicated FM software, document procedures in a Financial Management Manual, and conduct annual external audits.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial.

gen_risks.description: Focusing resources on digital channels and urban Citizen Service Centers risks reducing access and service quality for poor, vulnerable, elderly, and rural citizens.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish assisted digital access points, maintain non-digital information distribution, upgrade local agency front offices, and collect disaggregated beneficiary feedback.
gen_risks.evidence: there is a risk that the focus on state-of-the-art means for service delivery... will diminish access of the poor and vulnerable

gen_risks.description: The highly ambitious reform timeline creates schedule pressure for process re-engineering, legal amendments, and front-office rollouts across multiple agencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Sequence activities across three phases, incentivize milestones via Results-Based Financing DLIs over five years, and provide targeted technical assistance.
gen_risks.evidence: The Government's timeline for the reform is very ambitious.

gen_risks.description: Complex inter-sectoral coordination across more than a dozen participating line ministries and service delivery agencies may create implementation bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize the Prime Minister's Delivery Unit and high-level Inter-Ministerial Committees to oversee cross-agency alignment and resolve operational roadblocks.
gen_risks.evidence: Inter-sectoral reforms, especially those that involve more than a dozen government agencies, necessarily entail complex coordination.

gen_risks.description: Bureaucratic resistance from agency civil servants against ceding front-office customer service functions to ADISA and CSCs could impede reform execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement an active internal change management and communications campaign to align stakeholder incentives and cultivate reform champions in line agencies.
gen_risks.evidence: Ministries, agencies and individual civil servants may not welcome ceding the front office function to CSC. Bureaucratic resistance could stifle efforts

gen_risks.description: Incomplete, paper-based, or non-interoperable legacy data registers prevent effective business process re-engineering and service automation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Digitize archived paper records, validate national ID numbers, re-engineer administrative processes, and connect registers to the Government Interoperability Platform.
gen_risks.evidence: Property and pension records, for example, are only partially digitized.

gen_risks.description: Modest national internet penetration rates limit the rapid direct uptake of online e-government services by the general public.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain physical service points through ADISA customer service centers and provide assisted digital access points in post offices and local government units.
gen_risks.evidence: there will be a need for a physical presence where citizens can access services in person for the foreseeable future given modest levels of internet penetration

gen_risks.description: Delay in achieving global prerequisite DLI#5 (approval of Strategic Plan and completion of baseline survey) prevents any RBF disbursements under the loan.
gen_risks.mitigation: Use Project Preparation Facility (PPF) funding to rapidly complete the baseline survey and obtain Strategic Planning Committee approval for the Reform Policy Document.
gen_risks.evidence: This is a 'global' DLI, which means that no disbursements under the RBF component will be made until DLI#5 is met.

gen_risks.description: Long-term financial sustainability challenges regarding ongoing operating costs, software licenses, and required periodic IT system upgrades.
gen_risks.mitigation: Capture administrative savings from process re-engineering and ensure recurring O&M and software license expenses are integrated into national agency budgets.
gen_risks.evidence: Ongoing operating costs are expected to include licenses and system operation and maintenance. To continue efficiency improvements... Government will have to upgrade periodically.

gen_risks.description: Lack of specialized technical skills within public authorities to design, optimize, and maintain advanced IT systems and performance management tools.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy Technical Assistance loan funds to hire expert ICT advisors, database architects, and provide hands-on capacity building for agency personnel.
gen_risks.evidence: the authorities do not have staff with the technical skills and experience needed to implement the reform process.

gen_risks.description: Inaccuracy or misrepresentation in official administrative data failing to reflect true citizen-end processing delays and user experience.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct periodic independent citizen surveys, mandate third-party DLI verification, and implement real-time proactive text-message feedback mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: While administrative data record time necessary to obtain selected services, often administrative data does not reflect citizens' experience.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity poses challenges to delivering the reform effort, despite very high leadership commitment and fast-paced GoA initiation of reforms.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project Preparation Facility (PPF) is designed to assist capacity building for the implementing agency; the TA part of the loan continues building capacity to deliver, addressing the most pressing capacity needs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risks related to the new form of financial instrument used in Albania.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the fiduciary risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk, named alongside the fiduciary risk as being addressed by the same TA support (fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU); not separately elaborated beyond this.
gt_risks.mitigation: The TA part of the loan helps mitigate the technical design risk by supporting fiduciary and budget specialists in the PMU.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholder risks arising from inter-agency coordination.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by strong emphasis on coordination mechanisms in the design of the operation.

gt_risks.description: Bureaucratic resistance to enhanced transparency and simplification of administrative processes.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated in part through high-level leadership and engagement, and through citizen feedback arrangements that help pinpoint poor performance and corruption.

gt_risks.description: Political cycle risk from elections coming up in 2017, which could disrupt reform continuity and government commitment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Mitigated by making early progress in showing results and ensuring a broad constituency of support for the project's objectives and activities among the leadership of participating institutions and service users.
